Traffic paths and network explanations

Unit 1 · Week 14 · Lesson 1 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Open the network-review chapter and its learning resources. Use paper or a local editor as appropriate, with fictional data and disposable practice copies. The suggested 55-minute lesson is flexible.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Traffic paths and network explanations

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Explain the goal and the expected independent outcome. Explain a path using addressing and device functions. This is ungraded textbook learning. Suggested times can be adjusted to the class. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

2. Retrieval and explanation

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual retrieval, then partner comparison

A basic switch forwards local frames. The client ordinarily uses the gateway for off-subnet destinations under its mask. Allow silent thinking before discussion. Ask a learner to justify an answer before revealing the explanation. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

3. Two library destinations

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked table and teacher explanation

Use full addresses in the spoken explanation. A remote example such as 198.51.100.20 is fictional documentation data, not a live target. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

4. A complete explanation

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Predict, model and explain

Model the link between the requirement, mask comparison and routing action. A device name alone does not explain the outcome. Pause for predictions before discussing the expected result. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

5. Local and remote traces

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Guided paired practice

The wireless trace adds the access point. The remote destination adds the gateway/routing role. Keep the physical drawing consistent with the explanation. Swap explaining and checking roles so both learners articulate the reasoning. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

6. Independent practice

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent application with optional support

Use need, device, action and outcome as a writing scaffold. Learners then revise independently. Offer the relevant worked example if needed, then use a changed case to check independent understanding. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

7. A choice to explain

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Whole-class response and justification

A. Do not confuse the presence of a router with a requirement to route every local exchange. Give thinking time and collect reasons, without recording scores. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

8. Exit explanation

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual reflection and fresh explanation

Require the actual network comparison and gateway role. Use the response to select the next explanation or practice activity. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#network-review.
